question: A 76-year-old man is brought to the hospital after having a stroke. Head CT is done in the emergency department and shows intracranial hemorrhage. Upon arrival to the ED he is verbally non-responsive and withdraws only to pain. He does not open his eyes. He is transferred to the medical ICU for further management and intubated for airway protection. During his second day in the ICU, his blood pressure is measured as 91/54 mmHg and pulse is 120/min. He is given fluids and antibiotics, but he progresses to renal failure and his mental status deteriorates. The physicians in the ICU ask the patient’s family what his wishes are for end-of-life care. His wife tells the team that she is durable power of attorney for the patient and provides appropriate documentation. She mentions that he did not have a living will, but she believes that he would want care withdrawn in this situation, and therefore asks the team to withdraw care at this point. The patient’s daughter vehemently disagrees and believes it is in the best interest of her father, the patient, to continue all care. Based on this information, what is the best course of action for the physician team?

options.opa: Listen to the patient’s wife’s wishes and withdraw care
options.opb: Listen to the patient’s daughter’s wishes and continue all care
options.opc: Compromise between the wife and daughter and withdraw the fluids and antibiotics but keep the patient intubated
options.opd: Consult the hospital ethics committee and continue all care until a decision is reached
options.ope: Call other family members and consult them for their opinions

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient's wife is durable power of attorney" -> "Wife expresses desire to withdraw care" -> "Patient's daughter disagrees and wants to continue care" -> "Conflict arises between family members" -> "Ethical considerations regarding patient autonomy and family wishes" -> "Consulting the hospital ethics committee may provide guidance" -> "Continuing all care until a decision is reached" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient is in critical condition with deteriorating status" -> "Wife believes patient would want care withdrawn" -> "Daughter believes in continuing care" -> "Family dynamics complicate decision-making" -> "Ethics committee can mediate family disagreements" -> "Best course of action is to consult ethics committee" -> "Continue all care until a decision is reached" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient's condition is critical with renal failure" -> "Wife has durable power of attorney" -> "Wife's wishes conflict with daughter's wishes" -> "Patient's wishes are unclear due to lack of living will" -> "Ethical dilemma regarding end-of-life care" -> "Consulting ethics committee is appropriate" -> "Continue all care until a decision is reached" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient's wife requests withdrawal of care" -> "Daughter insists on continuing care" -> "Family disagreement on end-of-life decisions" -> "Wife's authority as power of attorney is valid" -> "Patient's wishes are not explicitly known" -> "Ethics committee can help resolve conflict" -> "Continue all care until a decision is reached" -> 75%
analysis: In this scenario, the patient is unable to express his wishes due to his medical condition, and the decision-making falls to his wife, who is the durable power of attorney. While the daughter disagrees with the wife's interpretation of the patient's wishes, the legal authority of the wife as the designated decision-maker should take precedence. The ethical principle of respecting the autonomy of the patient, as interpreted by the designated surrogate, supports the wife's request to withdraw care. Consulting the ethics committee could be beneficial in complex cases, but given the clear designation of the wife as the decision-maker, the best course of action is to honor her wishes. Therefore, the most appropriate option is to listen to the patient’s wife’s wishes and withdraw care.
